title: Relative exponentials convert cartesian transport to cocartesian precomposition
statement:
Let $S$ and $B$ be small quasicategories and let $p:B\to S$ be a cartesian fibration [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. Let $\mathscr A$ be a quasicategory in a containing universe [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Define $q:Q\to S$ by declaring an $n$-simplex of $Q$ to be a pair
$$\sigma:\Delta^n\to S,\qquad h:\Delta^n\times_S B\to\mathscr A.$$
Its operators are pullback along maps of standard simplices and restriction of $h$. Equivalently, for every simplicial set $K\to S$ there is a natural bijection
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{/S}(K,Q)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{sSet}}(K\times_S B,\mathscr A).$$
Then $Q$ is a quasicategory, $q$ is a cocartesian fibration, and its fibre over $s$ is $\operatorname{Fun}(B_s,\mathscr A)$. An edge $(\sigma,h)$ of $Q$ is $q$-cocartesian exactly when $h$ carries every cartesian edge of $\Delta^1\times_S B\to\Delta^1$ to an equivalence in $\mathscr A$.

source.place: Corollary 3.2.2.13, printed p. 187 (PDF p. 205), specialized to Y = S × A; its cocartesian edges are exactly those whose A-component is an equivalence. Compare the opposite-category dual of Kerodon Corollary 5.3.6.9 (Tag 0472). The degreewise fibre formula is the displayed relative Hom formula at a constant vertex. WANTED: archived HTT and Kerodon.

proof.text: An operator $\theta:[m]\to[n]$ sends $(\sigma,h)$ to $(\sigma\theta,h\circ(\Delta^m\times_S B\to\Delta^n\times_S B))$. Identity and composition hold on both coordinates. For a map $K\to S$, a map $K\to Q$ over $S$ assigns to each simplex $\tau:\Delta^n\to K$ its map $\Delta^n\times_S B\to\mathscr A$, compatibly on all operators; these glue degreewise to a map $K\times_S B\to\mathscr A$. Restriction is the inverse operation. This proves the natural displayed bijection.

source.place: Agent argument; Relative-Hom construction preceding Corollary 3.2.2.13; degreewise verification. Online mathematical reference only; archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Given an inner-horn lifting square for $q$, with $0<i<n$, and its prescribed base simplex $\sigma:\Delta^n\to S$, the bijection of step 1 turns it into the extension of a map $\Lambda_i^n\times_S B\to\mathscr A$ along the inclusion $j:\Lambda_i^n\times_S B\hookrightarrow\Delta^n\times_S B$. Reversing the vertex order of every simplex identifies $(\Lambda_i^n\subseteq\Delta^n)^{\mathrm{op}}$ with $\Lambda_{n-i}^n\subseteq\Delta^n$, again an inner horn inclusion, hence a trivial cofibration and in particular a categorical equivalence by [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure]. Reversal exchanges $\Lambda_0^m$ with $\Lambda_m^m$ and initial with final edges in the definitions of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], so $p^{\mathrm{op}}:B^{\mathrm{op}}\to S^{\mathrm{op}}$ is a cocartesian fibration of quasicategories. Apply [lem-coef-cocartesian-categorical-base-change] to $r=p^{\mathrm{op}}$, $b=\sigma^{\mathrm{op}}$ and $u$ the reversed horn inclusion: $u_{B^{\mathrm{op}}}=j^{\mathrm{op}}$ is a categorical equivalence. Reversal preserves and reflects categorical equivalences: reindexing $\Delta^m\cong(\Delta^m)^{\mathrm{op}}$ gives $\operatorname{Fun}(Y^{\mathrm{op}},C)\cong\operatorname{Fun}(Y,C^{\mathrm{op}})^{\mathrm{op}}$ naturally in $Y$, the homotopy category of an opposite is the opposite category, and $C^{\mathrm{op}}$ runs through all quasicategories with $C$. Hence $j$ is a degreewise injective categorical equivalence, a trivial cofibration of the Joyal model structure of [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure], formed in the universe containing $\mathscr A$. Since $\mathscr A$ is a quasicategory it is fibrant there, so the lifting axiom gives a strict extension. Thus $q$ is an inner fibration. To fill an absolute inner horn in $Q$, first fill its image in the quasicategory $S$, and then apply this relative lifting property to that chosen base simplex. Hence $Q$ is a quasicategory.

source.place: Agent argument; flatness of cartesian fibrations for inner horns via the opposite of Kerodon Corollary 5.6.7.6 (Tag 029H) and the Joyal model structure (HTT 2.2.5.1, 2.4.6.1); compare HTT 3.3.1.3. Online mathematical reference only; archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: We will use marked cofibrations to retain compatible extensions. Write $T_n$ for the degenerate edges and the edge $[0,1]$ of $\Delta^n$, $n\geq1$. The inclusion $(\Lambda_0^n,T_n|_{\Lambda_0^n})\to(\Delta^n,T_n)$ is a marked coanodyne generator, including $\Lambda_0^1=\{0\}$. For every marked simplicial set $V$, its product with $V$ is marked coanodyne: reverse the simplices to the marked-anodyne convention and apply the pushout-product assertion of [lem-coef-marked-anodyne-lifting-calculus] to $\varnothing\to V^{\mathrm{op}}$. Reversing back gives the assertion. Such maps, and their pushouts, are trivial cofibrations in the marked model structure over a point. Indeed the cited calculus makes restriction on $\operatorname{Map}^\sharp(-,C^\natural)$ a trivial Kan fibration for each quasicategory $C$ in the marked-anodyne convention; reversal gives the same test with $C^{\mathrm{op}}$. Reversal preserves weak homotopy equivalences by reversing barycentric coordinates in realizations. The weak-equivalence definition and lifting classes of the point model structure give the claimed trivial cofibrations and their stability under pushout.

source.place: Agent argument; Marked horn generators (3.1.1.1), pushout products (3.1.2.3), and the point model structure (3.1.3.7). Online mathematical reference only; archival copy WANTED.

proof.text:
Fix $\sigma:\Delta^n	o S$, $n\geq1$, and put $X=\Delta^n	imes_S B$. It is a cartesian fibration over $\Delta^n$: an inner lifting problem and a final-horn problem for an edge both project to the corresponding problem in $B$ with the same prescribed base simplex, and a cartesian lift in $B$ pairs with the prescribed base edge. By [lem-coef-cartesian-mapping-simplex-presentation] choose a chain $A_0\leftarrow\cdots\leftarrow A_n$ and a marked map $r:M^m(A)	o X^
atural$ over $\Delta^n$ which is a categorical equivalence on every vertex fibre. Put $M=M^m(A)$, $K=\Lambda_0^n$, and give $M,X$ the markings of [lem-cbc-cartesian-mapping-simplex-comparison] for $(\Delta^n,T_n)$ and $M_K,X_K$ those for $(K,T_n\cap K_1)$; thus $X$ is marked by its cartesian edges above $T_n$, and $X_K$ carries the induced marking. A simplex $(\alpha,a)$ of $M$ lies outside $M_K$ exactly when the image of $\alpha$ contains $\{1,\ldots,n\}$; then $\alpha(r)=n$ and $a\in(A_n)_r$. The map $A_n	imes\Delta^n	o M$, $(a,\alpha)\mapsto(\alpha,\varphi(a))$ with $\varphi:A_n	o A_{\alpha(r)}$ the composite chain transition, is simplicial by the operator formula of the mapping simplex, carries $A_n	imes K$ into $M_K$, and is bijective on the remaining simplices. Hence $M$ is the pushout of $M_K\leftarrow A_n	imes K	o A_n	imes\Delta^n$. An edge outside $M_K$ exists only for $n=1$, namely $(\mathrm{id},b)$ with $b\in(A_1)_1$, and it is marked exactly when $b$ is degenerate; the product edges with degenerate $A_n$-coordinate over $T_n$ go to marked edges. So, as marked simplicial sets, $M_K	o M$ is the pushout of $$A_n^ lat	imes(\Lambda_0^n,T_n|_K)\longrightarrow A_n^ lat	imes(\Delta^n,T_n).$$ This includes $n=1$, where $M_K=A_0$. Step 3 makes this a trivial cofibration over a point. In the commuting square from $M_K	o M$ to $X_K	o X$, both restrictions of $r$ are weak equivalences by [lem-cbc-cartesian-mapping-simplex-comparison], so two-out-of-three makes $X_K	o X$ a weak equivalence. It is a monomorphism with the induced marking and hence a trivial cofibration. Fibrancy of $\mathscr A^
atural$ now gives an exact marked extension $X	o\mathscr A^
atural$ of every marked map $X_K	o\mathscr A^
atural$. Thus the extension agrees with all of the given horn simultaneously; no pointwise gluing of chosen fillers is being assumed.

source.place: Agent argument; mapping-simplex presentation and its restriction to the initial horn (HTT 3.2.2.1, 3.2.2.7, 3.2.2.14, as in the proof of 3.2.2.12); explicit last-cylinder pushout. Online mathematical reference only; archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Call an edge of $Q$ special when it satisfies the edge condition in the statement. A cartesian edge above a degenerate base edge is an equivalence in the corresponding fibre: restrict its final-horn lifting property to constant base simplices and use the converse outer-horn criterion of [lem-cbc-equivalence-outer-horn-filling]. Every simplicial map preserves its inverse-triangle witnesses. Consequently in step 4 with $n=1$, an arbitrary $F:B_s\to\mathscr A$ is a marked map on $X_{\{0\}}$; the resulting marked extension is an edge of $Q$ over the given $\alpha:s\to t$, with source exactly $F$, and is special. For $n\geq2$, a horn in $Q$ whose first edge is special transposes to a marked map $X_K\to\mathscr A^\natural$: markings above $[0,1]$ are cartesian edges of $X\to\Delta^n$, hence cartesian for $\Delta^1\times_{\Delta^n}X=\Delta^1\times_S B\to\Delta^1$ (a final-horn problem there maps to one for $X$ with the same base, whose filler pairs with that base), and are respected by specialness and markings above degenerate edges by the preceding fibre observation. Step 4 extends it. By the horn definition, every special edge is $q$-cocartesian. The existence just proved for every source and every base edge, together with step 2, makes $q$ a cocartesian fibration.

source.place: Agent argument; Marked initial-horn lifting argument for Corollary 3.2.2.12, specialized to a quasicategory target over a point. Online mathematical reference only; archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: At a vertex $s$, the degree-$n$ fibre consists of maps $\Delta^n\times B_s\to\mathscr A$, with operators in the simplex factor. Interchanging factors identifies this degreewise, with all operators, with $\operatorname{Fun}(B_s,\mathscr A)$. It is a quasicategory as a fibre of the inner fibration $q$ over a vertex: lift each inner horn over the constant base simplex. No additional functor-category closure theorem is needed.

source.place: Agent argument; Fibre formula from the relative-Hom construction at a constant simplex. Online mathematical reference only; archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Finally let $e:F\to G$ be any $q$-cocartesian edge over $\alpha:s\to t$. Step 5 provides a special edge $e':F\to H$ over the same $\alpha$. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-composition-initiality] to the inner fibration $q$ of quasicategories: its two initial lifts have a comparison equivalence. In its explicit lift-category convention this gives a fibre equivalence $v:G\to H$ and a $2$-simplex with edges $e,v,e'$ over the degenerate base triangle $(\alpha,\mathrm{id}_t,\alpha)$. Under step 6, $v$ is an equivalence in $\operatorname{Fun}(B_t,\mathscr A)$; the pointwise criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] makes every $v(b_t)$ an equivalence. For a cartesian edge $a:b_s\to b_t$ of $\Delta^1\times_S B$, evaluate the transposed triangle on its degeneracy repeating the last vertex. The resulting triangle in $\mathscr A$ has edges $h_e(a)$, $v(b_t)$, $h_{e'}(a)$. The last edge is an equivalence by specialness. Composition and inverse-triangle homotopies in [lem-cbc-simplicial-composition-spine] show $h_e(a)$ is an equivalence too: compose the triangle with an inverse of $v(b_t)$, so its homotopy class is the product of two invertible classes, with inverse and both triangle witnesses furnished by the cited coherent composition. Edges over degenerate edges of $\Delta^1$ are already equivalences by step 5. Thus $e$ is special. Together with the sufficiency in step 5 this proves exactly the stated edge criterion.
